c: Check freshness: bright bulging eyes, red gills, firm flesh, sea smell; core ≤ 2 °C.
Scale tail-to-head under running water in a sink or bag; cut fins with scissors; rinse cavity, remove bloodline.
Fillet: cut behind the head to the bone, run the knife along the backbone head-to-tail, lift over the rib cage; repeat other side.
Trim belly and rib bones; pin-bone with tweezers along the lateral line (pull towards the head).
Portion 130 g (20 portions); score skin 3 times if pan-frying.
Bones + heads (gills removed) → fumet same day; trim → fish cakes or staff meal.
Record yield: target 42–45% skin-on fillet from gutted fish; below 40% = retrain or check supplier size.

c: Cut off fins with scissors 1 cm from the body; remove head with a V-cut behind it (keep for stock).
Four-fillet method: cut along the centre line to the bone, then lift each quarter fillet towards the edge; both sides.
Skin: hold tail end, knife at 15° between skin and flesh, pull skin while sawing.
Fillets: portion 150 g (16 portions); or cut 300 g bone-in tronçons across the fish for roasting.
Bones, head (gills removed) and frames: soak 1 h in iced water, fumet the same day (gelatin-rich).

c: Pull head and tentacles from the tube; cut tentacles just above the eyes; squeeze out the beak.
Remove the quill (pen) and innards from the tube; peel the purple membrane and wings; rinse.
Keep ink sacs (silver pouch) intact in a container for risotto or pasta (freeze in small portions).
Cut open tubes; score inside in a fine crosshatch (curls on cooking, tender bite).
Rule: cook < 2 min very hot or > 45 min slow; never in between (rubbery).
Optional brine 3% salt 20 min, or freeze −18 °C 48 h (breaks fibres). Target yield 68–72%.

c: Accept at ≤ 4 °C (bivalves 2–6 °C), with health mark and harvest tag; keep tags 90 days.
Reject gaping shells that do not close when tapped, cracked shells, strong smell, limp lobster/crab.
Bivalves: cold room 2–4 °C, in nets or trays, covered with a damp cloth; never in water or sealed bags; oysters cup-down.
Lobster/crab: 4–8 °C in a wet cloth or seaweed, 24 h max; no fresh water (kills them).
Clams: purge 1 h in 3% salted cold water before cooking; mussels: debeard just before cooking.
Lobster/crab: chill to torpor in the freezer 20 min (−18 °C), then stun or split through the head cross mark in one stroke before cooking; never cook conscious.
Discard bivalves that stay closed after cooking; cook mussels to 3–4 min open shell (core ≥ 75 °C).
Raw oysters: allergen + raw-food notice on menu; serve within 30 min of opening.

c: Chill crabs 20 min in the freezer; dispatch (pierce the nerve centres under the tail flap) immediately before cooking.
Boil in sea-salted water (30 g/L): 15 min first kg + 5 min each 500 g after; ice-water bath 5 min; drain upside down.
Twist off claws and legs; crack claws with the back of a heavy knife; pick white meat with a pick.
Remove the body (purse) from the shell; discard gills (dead man's fingers) and stomach sac; scoop brown meat.
Split the body; pick white meat from the chambers; run fingers through all meat twice for shell.
Target yield: 20–25% white meat, 10–12% brown meat; shells → crab bisque or stock.
